summary: Identify the pinned authorization rule artifact by the digest of its canonical JSON so a CRLF checkout resolves it, ending the Windows CI failure on every push since 2026-09-09.
why: GitHub CI on main failed on every push since 2026-09-09 17:06Z. Runs 34380853031, 34385335112, 34392699748 and 34396370729 fail only in 'Windows recon (Python 3.12)'; the four Linux jobs of 34396370729 pass. Git for Windows checks src/malleus/authorization-control-v1.json out with CRLF, so SHA-256 over the raw bytes is ba099f78b17488f9e811168f7e098518e7a2c5b997a4411d164c6564b19a880f, not the pinned identity, and importing malleus raises ControlError at control.py:51. That byte identity arrived in a7c54fa8, first pushed inside 74c715b4..82b33967; the last green run is 34291242305 at 74c715b4. OutcomeControlRules.from_bytes now parses first and digests the canonical JSON (compact separators, sorted keys, no NaN, UTF-8), the grammar malleus.ledger.canonical_json uses, so AUTHORIZATION_CONTROL_IDENTITY is re-derived from sha256:2164015909de89d798c80432b9239016b439cf56da54e33a56dd6a8b92d6817a to sha256:4f100b62dbdc444f240327d6dc26eac3764409d83ba875db73692d4e1aaac37e. Rule content, version-1 policy and evaluation hashes are unchanged. The guard is the test: RED 3d79de8c accepts the artifact from committed bytes and from the same bytes with CRLF. Windows stays unverified locally.
